newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Peters details ideas on NZ savings scheme limits.
newsitem.headline: Peters details ideas on NZ savings scheme limits.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters said on Tuesday that the country's planned new compulsory pension scheme might include a cap on the maximum level of savings at NZ$160,000 per person, which would buy an annuity equivalent to the current level of state-funded superannuation.
He also said the government would be prepared to top up savings which fell short of that target.

"Right now, the equivalent of what you pay people in terms of superannuation would amount to a annuity of a NZ$160,000 savings amount," Peters told the Association of Investment Advisers and Financial Planners.
He said the scheme would top up a person who had only managed to save, say, $130,000.
"That gives a far greater degree of certainty and a more comfortable income than, in my view, anything...under the current scheme," he said.
Peters said a consideration of the design team working on the savings plan was whether to have a scheme where people had to save regardless of the amounts they reached, such as in Singapore.

"Or is it wiser to have a cap that you simply save to, adjust that every five years to realities -- $160,000 this year may not be $160,000 in five years' time but it will be pretty near -- and above that the person can say 'well, I bow out now, I've saved my amount. I've put it aside and I've saved my money'?" Peters said.
